email.subject: Covering the migration remainder
email.body:
Phil,

The Micronaut 4 post called out a real platform cost: when agents ran from laptops, sleep or a dropped Wi-Fi connection broke the loop, so the team moved them onto self-hosted Cursor agents. That layer still has to be run and maintained for the remainder.

A useful next step is the work the post already flagged: services whose test suites let agent PRs through, and the rest of the Micronaut 4 cutover. Itaú ran a 6x faster .NET to Java migration of 59 services with Devin.

Open to 20 minutes on covering what's left?

drafts.linkedin_note: Phil, read the Micronaut 4 post on moving agents off laptops. I work on Devin; we can take remaining services and test gaps without asking platform to rebuild the harness. Glad to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Phil, one more from the migration post: a few automated PRs passed all existing unit and integration tests and still caused subtle runtime bugs, because some services had gaps in their test suites. That remainder, plus harness upkeep, is the useful next wave alongside the pipeline you just published. Itaú used Devin to take test coverage from ~50% to ~90+%. If useful, I can share how they sequenced it next to an existing agent setup.
